captions.instagram:
How does a mixer grinder work?

A motor that spins 20,000 times a minute, blades whose tips hit 200 km/h, and ribs that stop your chutney riding round the jar. Take India's favourite kitchen machine apart in 3D.

→ A mixer grinder is a very fast motor in the base, and a jar of blades on top.
→ On AC the current flips 100 times a second, in the magnet and the armature together, so the push never changes direction.
→ Load the blades and the motor slows down, draws more current and gets hotter.
→ The blade tip is only 3.5 cm from the centre, but at 17,000 rpm it moves at over 220 km/h.
→ Each hit breaks bits smaller: fast at first, then slower, as every step needs more energy.

youtubeLong.title: How does a mixer grinder work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A motor that spins 20,000 times a minute, blades whose tips hit 200 km/h, and ribs that stop your chutney riding round the jar. Take India's favourite kitchen machine apart in 3D.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/mixerclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/mixerclear

In this video:
• A fast motor under a jar of blades. A mixer grinder is a heavy base holding an upright electric motor, with a jar on top.
• A motor that runs on AC because both halves flip. The universal motor sends the same current through its field coils and, via carbon brushes and a commutator, through its spinning armature.
• Tiny blades, racing-car tip speed. The tip speed of a blade is v = ω × r.
• Ribs stop the whole load spinning. On its own, the load swirls round with the blade, forming a vortex, and the blade slips through food that is already moving.
• Every watt ends up as heat. Current heats the windings, and the work done on the food heats the food: Q = P × t.
• A gram of imbalance shakes it hard. A lump spinning with the blade pulls on the machine with F = m r ω².
